description: This set of three pie charts illustrates the distribution of problem types categorized by difficulty—easy, medium, and hard—across two conditions: with knowledge (N+K+) and without knowledge (N−K+), as well as their combinations with and without chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, represented by the four segments in each chart. Each pie chart is divided into four colored segments corresponding to the legend: teal for N+K+, yellow for N−K+, orange for N−K−, and red for N+K−. The easy chart shows N+K+ at 40.6%, N−K+ at 45.9%, N−K− at 10.1%, and N+K− at 3.3%. The medium chart displays N+K+ at 44.6%, N−K+ at 44.3%, N−K− at 7.2%, and N+K− at 3.9%. The hard chart shows N+K+ at 20.1%, N−K+ at 36.2%, N−K− at 36.8%, and N+K− at 7.0%. All percentages within each pie chart sum to 100%. The charts are presented side-by-side with the difficulty level as a title above each, and the overall label “CoT” is centered below them. The legend is positioned to the right of the hard chart, and no slices are exploded or visually emphasized. The segments appear to be arranged in descending order of size within each chart.
